coherence.reasons: Both build the same sound hierarchy: recommendation, then B fails the board's tests, then A passes on plan but payback is fragile, then gates. X's question-led structure is tight, and it places the payback condition (ACoS at or below 28.6%) in the governing thought itself. But X contradicts itself at evidence level. It calls $3.9M the "worst-case peak cash need" while its own stall case ends at -$6.8M and its 38% ACoS case at -$6.4M. Its backup says to "use 32%" ACoS, at which its own model misses payback, while the approval is framed as passing on plan with a 28.6% ceiling. Y's summary, titles and tables agree throughout (the $5M envelope is tied to a named scenario, and it says the 38% case would exceed it). Y's own tension is that it re-bases the plan at 30–32% ACoS, where payback slips past 2030, but it states this openly. X's stronger top-level framing and Y's cleaner internal consistency roughly offset.

judgment.reasons: Both reach the key's preferred conclusion: Amazon-led with gates, retail rejected, the $40M ambition reset. Y weighs the trade-offs more fully. It tests volume as well as ACoS (at 80% of plan A only just pays back, at 70% it misses), so the board sees payback depends on two things, not one. It treats Japan in the main body and concedes that at 32% ACoS Japan beats A on cash (+$1.8M against -$2.3M), then argues for the US on strategic grounds and schedules a 2028 Japan case. It sizes a $5M cash envelope to a named downside and says which case would breach it. It adds a repeat-purchase trigger, a door-test gate and a margin-affordability gate for later retail. X adds a useful stall case (-$6.8M) with an end-2027 stop rule, and makes resetting the ambition an explicit board decision. But X treats ACoS as something a "cap" can hold while volumes stay fixed, and weighs Japan mostly on revenue in a backup page. Y is also more candid that payback will probably slip at benchmark ad costs.

evidence.reasons: Both reproduce the key's numbers accurately: $4.73 and $7.55 per unit, $20.8M peak for B, 4.5% group margin, 28.6% break-even ACoS, the 25/28/32% payback pattern, the 26.9% ceiling under a 25% duty. Both reject the $5.2B figure, the 4.5 units per door and the correlation-based halo. Y uses more of the pack. It notes pilot month-on-month growth slowed from about 17% to 9%, which guards against extrapolating the pilot. It runs volume sensitivities and decomposes B's corrected cases (no halo, 2.6 units, both). It reads the interquartile range correctly. X has a few loose claims. "Demand grew without Onsoo pushing it" sits oddly with a 28% ACoS. "Worst-case peak cash need $3.9M" is contradicted by its own stall and 38% cases. Mooncrest is given a full slide as a pattern Option B "would repeat", though X does call it the one such entrant. X's stall case is a good use of the two stalled Amazon-first peers.

revision.reasons: Both keep the CEO's Amazon-first hypothesis with conditions, as the key expects. Both replace the 25% ACoS assumption, raise the retail awareness trigger from 15% to 20% using the 10–20% band median of 3.5 against the 4.0 cut-off, and reset the $40M timing. X sets this out in an explicit from-to slide covering trigger, ad cost, seller, downside, ambition and tariff. Y goes a step further on the second half of the hypothesis. It models the CEO's 2029 retail add-on at B's scale (cash -$11.8M, group margin 6.3%) and shows that even a well-gated retail move would break the margin floor and payback unless resized. It then adds door-test and affordability gates. That is a more substantive test of the hypothesis than X's change of trigger alone.

overall.reasons: Both documents would lead the board to the same defensible decision, on the same correct core numbers, and both meet all four defensibility criteria. Y serves the decision maker somewhat better. It is franker that payback is fragile on both ad cost and volume. It weighs Japan honestly and gives it a route back in 2028. It ties the cash ask to a specific downside scenario. It tests the CEO's later retail step against the constraints. X's distinctive strengths are the stall case with a stop rule and the explicit hypothesis from-to page. Against that, X labels $3.9M as worst case despite its own worse cases, and leans on an ACoS "cap" with volumes held fixed.
